title: Ordered restriction as a module cochain map
statement: Let $X',T'$ be schemes and $f':X'\to T'$ a morphism. Let $M$ be a module sheaf on $X'$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $W_i$, $i\in\operatorname{Fin}(r)$, any finite family of opens. Let $K$ be an integer cochain complex of module sheaves on $T'$ with zero negative terms. Suppose for all nonnegative $p$ and opens $B\subset T'$ there are additive equivalences $a_{p,B}:\Gamma(B,K^p)\simeq\prod_t\Gamma((\bigcap_lW_{t(l)})\cap(f')^{-1}B,M)$ indexed by increasing $(p+1)$-tuples [def-sc-alternating-cech-total-complex]. Assume these equivalences commute with restrictions of $B$, take multiplication by $b\in\Gamma(B,\mathcal O_{T'})$ to multiplication by the restriction of $(f')^*b$ on each coordinate, and intertwine $d_K$ with the signed face-restriction sum. Let $D$ be a nonnegative cochain complex of module sheaves on $X'$. Suppose its terms, after forgetting to presheaves of global-ring modules, are identified by natural isomorphisms $e_p$ with the usual all-tuple Cech terms of $W,M$. Assume $e$ intertwines differentials, and each coordinate on an open $C\subset X'$ takes multiplication by $b\in\Gamma(C,\mathcal O_{X'})$ to multiplication by its restriction to $(\bigcap_lW_{y(l)})\cap C$. Let $L=(f'_*D)^{\mathrm{ext}}$ and let $q$ be its ordered coordinate maps [def-pc-ordered-cech-module-coordinates]. There is a cochain map $R:L\to K$ of module sheaves such that $a_{p,B,t}(R(s))=q_{p,B,t}(s)$ for every nonnegative degree $p$, base open $B$, section $s$ and increasing tuple $t$. No signed extension or retraction identity is asserted.

source.place: Tags 01FJ and 01FK; Coherence part (a), restriction to increasing tuples and signed extension; comparison proof steps 1 and 2

proof.text: Evaluate e on inverse-image opens. Define R sectionwise by the inverse of a applied to the ordered coordinates q. The proved coordinate naturality and local scalar identity, with hn and hl, show that R is natural and locally linear. The face equations ha and hd identify its differential equation: deletion of an increasing entry is the corresponding usual Cech face, and the two intersection restriction composites are the unique maps between the same opens.

Set the negative components to zero. The source L has zero terms in every negative degree, so all chain equations with negative source, including -1 to 0, vanish. The inverse-equivalence identity gives the stated coordinate formula.
